summary: POC scoping focused on integrating BluePeak's inference scripts into Redwood's benchmark harness. Discussed load profiles (streaming vs non-streaming), success criteria (p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1000 tokens), timeline for running bench tests, and security docs needed for pilot.
transcript: Meeting header: 2026-05-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: ~55 minutes | Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai (Redwood) — Samir Patel, Laura Chen, Evan Rogers (BluePeak)
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. We're here to scope the POC and specifically the benchmark harness integration for your inference scripts. Quick intro?

00:12 Samir: Hi all, Samir from BluePeak. We're looking to validate latency at scale and cost for our summarization feature. We'll want p95 under 300ms for short conversations and throughput to hit our peak of ~150 rps.
00:28 Alex: Got it. Priya is our SE — she'll take the technical lead on the harness integration. Priya, quick overview?

00:35 Priya: Yep — hi. The bench harness is our repo that runs both streaming and non-streaming flows, can replay request traces, and measure token-level throughput and tail latencies. We'll need your inference scripts and a sample payload distribution to generate realistic load.
00:52 Laura: Quick question: do you run the tests from Redwood-hosted infra or do we run them inside our VPC? Security wants to know about egress and keys.

01:04 Priya: We can do both. For initial runs we usually run hosted to iterate faster; for production-like numbers we prefer running from a VPC with the Dedicated nodes. We'll provide a network diagram and KMS notes.
01:20 Evan: On the streaming vs non-streaming front — our production uses streaming for UX, but batch fallback exists. We need to understand cost delta and tail latency impact.

01:33 Priya: Streaming adds overhead on throughput but often reduces perceived latency for first token. Our harness supports streaming emulation — we can run paired tests: streaming to measure time-to-first-token and full completion times, and non-streaming for aggregate throughput and cost to completion.
01:50 Alex: For success criteria, how should we frame it? Examples we've seen: p95 latency < 300ms, p99 < 600ms for short texts; cost under $X per 1k tokens. What matters to you?
02:05 Samir: p95 is priority. Also CPUT/service concurrency limits — we want to ensure no tail spikes during peak. If Dedicated nodes are required to meet SLAs, we need clear cost estimates.

02:20 Priya: We'll instrument the harness to report p50/p95/p99, token throughput, and cost estimate using our model runtimes and instance pricing. We'll also capture CPU/GPU util to help tune batch sizes.
02:37 Laura: About scripts: our scripts include a preprocessing step that hits an internal service — can we stub that out?
02:45 Priya: Yes — the harness accepts a hook to run a preprocessor container or a stubbed response. If you can share a deterministic sample and the expected latencies, we can replay accurately.
03:00 Samir: We'll share two scripts: one representative streaming client (websocket-like) and one REST batch call. Expect ~70% streaming, 30% batch in production.
03:12 Alex: Great — that mix helps define the load profiles. Priya, recommended test matrix?

03:18 Priya: I suggest: (1) baseline single-node cold start tests, (2) sustained load at 25/50/75/100% of expected peak, (3) stress test to max RPS to find saturation, (4) streaming first-token latency tests under concurrency. We'll run each at least 5 minutes to warm KV cache and measure steady-state.
03:40 Evan: For warm KV cache — what's your warmup strategy? We don't want unrealistic cache hits.

03:46 Priya: Good call. We can run a prefix workload to pre-populate KV cache similar to your production trace; optionally we can disable prefix caching for a more conservative test. We'll collaborate on the sample traces.
03:58 Alex: On instrumentation — we'll publish the harness results as CSV + dashboards. We'll also attach raw logs for tail analysis. Any specific metrics you need beyond tokens and latency?
04:10 Samir: Perf counters per model variant, GPU util, queue depth, and error rates. Also, we'd like throughput per cost metric: tokens/sec per dollar.

04:22 Priya: We'll include model-level breakdowns and estimated cost per 1k tokens using both hosted and dedicated pricing assumptions. We'll also include a sensitivity analysis for batch size and quantization.
04:35 Laura: Security items — SOC2, SSO, tenant isolation details. Do you have an SOC2 report we can share with our security folks?
04:42 Alex: Yes, we'll send the SOC2 summary and our compliance packet. Priya will add network diagrams and KMS/HSM notes.
05:00 Samir: Timeline — we'd like to run the first set of benchmarks within two weeks. Is that feasible?

05:05 Priya: If we get scripts and a small sample dataset this week, we can prepare harness configs and start hosted runs next week. For VPC/Dedicated tests we'll need account setup and possibly firewall/NAT changes, which can add a week. So two weeks for hosted, three to four for VPC-level tests.
05:25 Evan: About model variants — we're experimenting with a smaller quantized model for cost reasons. Can the harness compare accuracy/regression vs a larger model?

05:33 Priya: Yes, we can run A/B runs. We'll calculate basic quality metrics (e.g., ROUGE or similarity scores) if you provide evaluation prompts/labels. We'll include output sampling to check hallucination rates too.
05:48 Alex: Any blockers for you to share scripts? Auth? Where do we want files?
05:55 Samir: We'll drop them in the shared folder in Drive and send access to Alex and Priya. There is an internal token in one script — we'll sanitize before upload.

06:05 Priya: Perfect. For the harness repo, we'll send a minimal README on how to plug your script — the input is a line-delimited JSON sample and a runner wrapper. We have example wrappers for websocket streaming and REST.
06:20 Laura: About load generation — do you recommend running Locust or your built-in generator?

06:26 Priya: We have an internal generator optimized for token-aware load and backpressure that simulates real client behavior (think pipelined streaming). For comparison we can run Locust or k6 but the built-in harness gives us better token-level fidelity.
06:40 Alex: Costing: we'll provide ballpark for hosted per-token and for Dedicated we'll show node-hour pricing + amortized per-token. We'll include burst options for peak.
06:52 Samir: Important: We need the p95 target for short texts and also a cost target — we can share internal cost ceilings. If you can show a path to meet both that's ideal.
07:03 Priya: We'll prepare a table: scenario -> expected p95/p99 -> estimated cost/1k tokens -> recommended config (dedicated vs hosted, batch sizes, quantization).
07:18 Evan: On observability, how granular are your traces? We want per-request IDs mapped to our trace IDs so we can correlate errors.

07:27 Priya: We can accept a trace_id header in requests and we'll surface that in logs. We'll also export an events file with latency broken down by model host, queue time, kernel exec time approximations.
07:42 Laura: One more on security: what about data retention during tests? We don't want logs to persist past 30 days.
07:49 Alex: We can configure retention per-project; we'll note the default and options for shorter retention. We'll include that in the packet.
08:00 Samir: So next steps recap? We want the harness repo + README, we'll upload scripts, agree on test window week of May 18, and get SOC2/docs.
08:12 Alex: Yep — I'll send the repo link and a proposed schedule after this call. Priya will produce the suggested load matrix. Priya, anything else?
08:20 Priya: I'll also send two example configs (streaming-heavy and non-streaming-heavy) and a baseline recommended batch size and quantization profile to test.
08:30 Evan: On logging — can you include occasional raw outputs so our PMs can sanity check generations?
08:35 Priya: We'll sample outputs at a configurable rate and attach to the results bundle. We'll redact PII if you ask.
08:44 Laura: Could you also include instructions for running tests from our VPC? We have a hardened environment so steps and ports are helpful.
08:52 Priya: Absolutely — network port list and a small terraform snippet to spin up a test agent in your VPC. We'll include that in the packet.
09:05 Samir: Any concerns about streaming scale? If we sustain 150 rps mostly streaming, will we run into connection limits?

09:13 Priya: Streaming requires more connection headroom. For high concurrent websockets we'd recommend dedicated pools and a load balancer with sticky sessions. We'll include recommended connection concurrency and autoscale knobs.
09:28 Alex: Pricing estimate — I'll draft a preliminary estimate for two dedicated nodes sized for your throughput and include a hosted fallback. Will send by Monday.
09:37 Evan: Great. If the first run looks good, what's the path to expand POC to include SSO and audit logging?
09:44 Alex: We can add SSO (SAML) integration during pilot; audit logs are available as an addon and we'll show how to push logs to your SIEM. That would be part of the enterprise checklist.

09:58 Priya: Final technical note: we will run both cold-start and warm cache experiments and provide a combined report. We recommend focusing on warm steady-state for production SLAs but cold-start is useful for burst patterns.
10:12 Samir: That works. We'll aim to have scripts and sample traces uploaded by Friday. We'll review the SOC2 packet and scheduling option.
10:20 Alex: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the repo link and schedule. Meeting adjourned.
